perspective:
Ethan’s available perspective:

- Ethan knows Gary is his long-time friend from middle school and works as a doctor; they have relied on each other for emotional and professional support.
- Ethan noticed Gary working excessively long hours, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep. He became concerned about Gary’s health.
- Ethan invited Gary to a two-day weekend retreat for relaxation. He heard Gary refuse, saying he appreciated the concern but couldn’t go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, Ethan observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. Ethan suspected there was more to Gary’s overworking than professional obligations.
- Ethan confronted Gary, saying they had been friends since middle school and that Gary could tell him anything without judgment.
- Gary told Ethan, “It’s complicated,” and that he didn’t want to burden Ethan with his problems.
- Gary later opened up to Ethan about pressures from managing a new department and personal challenges he was facing.
- Ethan suggested prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities. Gary agreed, saying he needed help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary. Gary told him things were better, he felt less overwhelmed, and he had had time for a movie the previous weekend.
- Ethan told Gary he was proud of his progress and that he was there whenever Gary needed to talk.
- After about a year, Ethan saw Gary managing a healthier work-life balance and appearing capable on his own. Ethan told Gary he was always just a call away but knew Gary had it handled.
- Gary thanked Ethan, said he couldn’t have done it without Ethan’s support, and said he felt more in control.
- Ethan’s own actions/feelings: he was concerned, invited Gary to the retreat, observed him there, confronted him, offered help, checked in regularly, felt relief/empathy/hope/proud/satisfied, and eventually stepped back while remaining available.
